newsitem.title: USA: Duff & Phelps may still cut Central Maine.
newsitem.headline: Duff & Phelps may still cut Central Maine.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co on Thursday said it would continue monitoring Central Maine Power Co for a possible downgrading of its debt rating after the announcement that the Maine Yankee nuclear power plant may be closed.

On Tuesday, Maine Yankee, which is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power, said it was considering permanently closing its 910-megawatt Maine Yankee nuclear power plant and would cut spending on the unit until a decision is made.
"In our view, the plant may be shut down because of viability concerns," Duff & Phelps said.
Duff & Phelps said the credit implications of a closure would depend on the change in Central Maine's cost structure, regulatory issues, replacement power and changes in public policy.
"The prospects for favorable resolution of these issues are not clear at this point and a final decision regarding the plant's status has yet to be made," the firm said.
"Continuation of our Rating Watch-Down status reflects this uncertainty and the potential for the above issues to negatively impact CTP's credit quality," it said.
